text: `between x y z` means `y` is between `x` and `z`

name: between_if
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point), between a b c → |(a─b)| + |(b─c)| = |(a─c)|
text: Transfer inferences defined in Sec. 3.6 of Avigad et al. 2009 diagram-segment transfer axioms If b is  between a and c, then ab + bc = ac. [between_if, equal_circles, point_on_circle_if, point_on_circle_onlyif, sum_angles_if, sum_angles_onlyif, perpendicudlar_if, sum_areas_if] Given any points a, b and c such that b is between a and c, then the straight-line from a to c is equal to the sum of the straight-lines from a to b and from b to c.

name: between_not_trans
statement: ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between a b d) → ¬(between c b d)
text: If b is  between a and c and b is  between a and d then b is not  between c and d

name: between_points
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a ≠ b) ∧ (b ≠ c) ∧ (c ≠ a) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) → (between a b c) ∨ (between b a c) ∨ (between a c b)
text: If a, b, and c are distinct points on a line L, then then either b is  between a and c, or a is a. between bnd c, or c is  between a and b

name: between_same_line_in
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) → b.onLine L
text: 3  If b is  between a and c, a is on L, and c is on L, then b is on L

name: between_same_line_out
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) → c.onLine L
text: If b is  between a and c, a is on L, and b is on L, then c is on L

name: between_symm
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point), between a b c → (between c b a) ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ ¬(between b a c)
text: between axioms If b is  between a and c then b is  between c and a, a != b, a != c, and a is not a. between bnd c

name: between_trans_in
statement: ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between a d b) → between a d c
text: If b is  between a and c and d is  between a and b then d is  between a and c

name: between_trans_out
statement: ∀ (a b c d : Point), (between a b c) ∧ (between b c d) → (between a b d)
text: If b is  between a and c and c is a. between bnd d then b is  between a and d

name: center_inside_circle
statement: ∀ (a : Point) (α : Circle), a.isCentre α → a.insideCircle α
text: If a is the centre of α then a is inside α

name: centre_unique
statement: ∀ (a b : Point) (α : Circle), (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.isCentre α) → a = b
text: If points `a` and `b` are both centers of `(α : Circle)` then `a = b`

name: circle_from_points
statement: ∀ (a b : Point), a ≠ b → ∃ α : Circle, (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.onCircle α)

name: circle_line_intersections
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line) (α : Circle), (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) ∧ (a.insideCircle α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (b ≠ c) → between b a c
text: circle axioms If a, b, and c are on L, a is inside α, b and c are on α, and b != c, then a -- is a. between bnd c

name: circle_points_between
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(b.outsideCircle α) ∧ (between a c b) → c.insideCircle α
text: If a and b are each inside α or on α, and c is  between a and b, then c is inside α

name: circle_points_extend
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(c.insideCircle α) ∧ (between a c b) → (b.outsideCircle α)
text: If a is inside α or on α, c is not inside α, and c is  between a and b, then b is neither inside α nor on α

name: circles_intersections_diff_side
statement: ∀ (a b c d : Point) (α β : Circle) (L : Line), (α ≠ β) ∧ (c.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle β) ∧ (d.onCircle α) ∧ (d.onCircle β) ∧ (c ≠ d) ∧ (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.isCentre β) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) → ¬(c.sameSide d L)
text: 4  Let α and β be distinct circles that intersect in distinct points c and d Let a be a the centre of α, let b be the centre of β, and let L be the line through a and b  Then c and d are not on the same side of L

name: collinear
statement: (a b c : Point) : Prop

name: degenerated_angle_if
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) ∧ ¬(between b a c) → ∠ b:a:c = 0
text: diagram-angle transfer axioms Suppose a != b, a != c, a is on L, and b is on L. Then c is on L and a is not  between b and c if and only if \bac = 0. Given points a, b and c such that a is not equal to b and a is not equal to c, and line L such that a, b, and c are all on L, and a is not between b and c, then the angle bac has degree zero.

name: degenerated_angle_onlyif
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (∠ b:a:c = 0) → (c.onLine L) ∧ ¬(between b a c)
text: Given points a, b and c such that a is not equal to b and a is not equal to c, and line L such that a and b are on L, and the angle formed by b:a:c has degree zero,  then c is on L and a is not between b and c.

name: degenerated_area
statement: ∀ (a b : Point), Triangle.area △ a:a:b = 0
text: △aab = 0. △ @[simp]

name: degenerated_area_if
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), distinctPointsOnLine a b L ∧ (Triangle.area △ a:b:c) = 0 → c.onLine L
text: diagram-area transfer axioms If a and b are on L and a != b, then △abc = 0 if and only if c is on L. If a and b are two distinct points both lying on a given line L, with a given a point c such that the area of the triangle abc is zero, then c must also be on L.

name: degenerated_area_onlyif
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), distinctPointsOnLine a b L ∧ (c.onLine L) → (Triangle.area △ a:b:c) = 0
text: If a and b are two distinct points both lying on a given line L, with a given a point c also lying on L, then the area of the triangle abc is zero

extra.definition: λ P Q L => P.onLine L ∧ Q.onLine L ∧ P ≠ Q

name: distinctPointsOnLine
statement: Point → Point → Line → Prop

name: distinct_point_same_side
statement: ∀ (L : Line) (b c : Point), ¬(b.onLine L) → ∃ a : Point, a ≠ c ∧ a.sameSide b L

name: distinct_points
statement: ∀ p₁ : Point, ∃ p₂ : Point, p₁ ≠ p₂

name: equal_angles
statement: ∀ (a b b' c c' : Point) (L M : Line), (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (b'.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (c'.onLine M) ∧ (b ≠ a) ∧ (b' ≠ a) ∧ (c ≠ a) ∧ (c' ≠ a) ∧ ¬(between b a b') ∧ ¬(between c a c') → (∠ b:a:c = ∠ b':a:c')
text: Suppose a, b, and b′ are on L, a, c, and c′ are on M, b != a, b′ != a, c != a, c′ != a, a is not  between b and b′, and a is not between c and c′. Then \bac = \b′ac′. -- Given points a, b, and b′ all on a given line L, and points c, c' such that a, c, and c′ are all on given line M, with b distinct from a, b′ distinct from a, c distinct from a, c' distinct from a, a is not  between b and b′, and a is not between c and c′, then angle bac is equal to angle b′ac′.

name: equal_circles
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (α β : Circle), (a.isCentre α) ∧ (a.isCentre β) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle β) ∧ |(a─b)| = |(a─c)| → α = β
text: If a is the centre of α and β, b is on α, c is on β, and ab = ac, then α = β. If a point x is the centre of two circles C and D, and given points b and d such that b is on C and c is on D and the straight-line from x to b is equal to the straight-line from x to c, then C is equal to D.

name: exists_distinct_point_inside_circle
statement: ∀ (α : Circle) (b : Point), ∃ a : Point, a ≠ b ∧ a.insideCircle α

name: exists_distinct_point_on_circle
statement: ∀ (α : Circle) (b : Point), ∃ a : Point, a ≠ b ∧ (a.onCircle α)

name: exists_distinct_point_opposite_side
statement: ∀ (L : Line) (b c : Point), ¬(b.onLine L) → ∃ a : Point, a ≠ c ∧ a.opposingSides b L

name: exists_distinct_point_outside_circle
statement: ∀ (α : Circle) (b : Point), ∃ a : Point, a ≠ b ∧ a.outsideCircle α

name: exists_distincts_points_on_line
statement: ∀ l : Line, ∀ p : Point, ∃ p' : Point, p ≠ p' ∧ p'.onLine l

name: exists_point_between_points_not_on_line
statement: ∀ (L M : Line) (b c : Point), distinctPointsOnLine b c L ∧ L ≠ M → ∃ a : Point, (a.onLine L) ∧ (between b a c) ∧ ¬(a.onLine M)

name: exists_point_between_points_on_line
statement: ∀ (L : Line) (b c : Point), distinctPointsOnLine b c L → ∃ a : Point, (a.onLine L) ∧ (between b a c)

name: exists_point_inside_circle
statement: ∀ (α : Circle), ∃ a : Point, a.insideCircle α

name: exists_point_on_circle
statement: ∀ (α : Circle), ∃ a : Point, a.onCircle α

name: exists_point_opposite
statement: ∀ (L : Line) (b : Point), ¬(b.onLine L) → ∃ a : Point, a.opposingSides b L

name: exists_point_outside_circle
statement: ∀ (α : Circle), ∃ a : Point, a.outsideCircle α

name: extend_point
statement: ∀ (L : Line) (b c : Point), distinctPointsOnLine b c L → ∃ a : Point, (a.onLine L) ∧ (between b c a)

name: extend_point_longer

text: This rule is not in [Avigad et al., 2009] but is convenient for proving some propositions.

name: extend_point_not_on_line

name: flat_angle_if
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point), a ≠ b ∧ b ≠ c ∧ ∠ a:b:c = ∟ + ∟ → between a b c
text: Given points a b and c with a distinct from b and b distinct from c, such that angle abc is the sum of two right angles, then b is between a and c /-- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] -/

name: flat_angle_onlyif
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point), between a b c → ∠ a:b:c = ∟ + ∟

statement: (a b c d : Point) (AB CD AC BD : Line) : Prop

statement: ∀ (a : Point) (α : Circle), a.insideCircle α → ¬(a.onCircle α)
text: If (a : Point) is inside (α : Circle), then a is not on α

name: intersection_circle_circle_1
statement: ∀ (a b : Point) (α β : Circle), (a.onCircle α) ∧ ¬(b.outsideCircle α) ∧ (a.insideCircle β) ∧ (b.outsideCircle β) → α.intersectsCircle β

name: intersection_circle_circle_2
statement: ∀ (a b : Point) (α β : Circle), (a.onCircle α) → (b.insideCircle α) → (a.insideCircle β) → (b.onCircle β) → α.intersectsCircle β
text: 5  If a is on α, b is in α, a is in β, and b is on β, then α and β intersect

name: intersection_circle_line_1
statement: ∀ (a b : Point) (α : Circle) (L: Line), ¬(a.outsideCircle α) ∧ ¬(b.outsideCircle α) ∧ (a.opposingSides b L) → L.intersectsCircle α
text: If a is on or inside α, b is on or inside α, and a and b are on different sides of L, then L and α intersect

name: intersection_circle_line_2
statement: ∀ (a : Point) (α : Circle) (L: Line), (a.insideCircle α) ∧ (a.onLine L) → L.intersectsCircle α

between a and c and b is on L then a and c are not on the same -- side of L -- ******** -- -- See also Avigad's notes on this rule (https://www.andrew.cmu.edu/user/avigad/Papers/euclid_notes.htm) meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points -- on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, -- and b and c are on the same side of N, and d and e are on the same side -- name: pasch_1
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.sameSide c L) → a.sameSide b L
text: If b is  between a and c and a and c are on the same side of L, then a and b are on the same side of L

name: pasch_2
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ ¬(b.onLine L) → b.sameSide c L
text: If b is  between a and c and a is on L and b is not on L, then b and c are on the same side of L

name: pasch_3
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (between a b c) ∧ (b.onLine L) → ¬(a.sameSide c L)
text: If b is  between a and c and b is on L then a and c are not on the same side of L -- See also Avigad's notes on this rule (https://www.andrew.cmu.edu/user/avigad/Papers/euclid_notes.htm)

name: pasch_4
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L M : Line), (L ≠ M) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine M) ∧ distinctPointsOnLine a c M ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (c ≠ b) ∧ ¬(a.sameSide c L) → between a b c
text: If b is the intersection of distinct lines L and M, a and c are distinct points on M, a != b, c != b, and a and c are not on the same side of L, then b is between a and c

name: perpendicular_if
statement: ∀ (a b c d : Point) (L : Line), (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (between a c b) ∧ ¬(d.onLine L) ∧ (∠ a:c:d = ∠ d:c:b) → ∠ a:c:d = ∟
text: Suppose a and b are points on L, c is  between a and b, and d is not on L. Then \acd = \dcb if and only if \acd is equal to right-angle. Given points a and b both lying on a given line L, and point c lying between a and b, and point d not on L such that the angle acd is equal to the angle dcb, then the angle acd is a right angle.

name: perpendicular_onlyif
statement: ∀ (a b c d : Point) (L : Line), (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (between a c b) ∧ ¬(d.onLine L) ∧ (∠ a:c:d = ∟) → ∠ a:c:d = ∠ d:c:b
text: Given points a and b both lying on a given line L, and point c lying between a and b, and point d not on L such that the angle acd is a right angle, then the angle acd is equal to the angle dcb.

name: point_between_points_shorter_than
statement: ∀ (L : Line) (b c : Point) (s : Segment), distinctPointsOnLine b c L ∧ (|s| > 0) → ∃ a : Point, (a.onLine L) ∧ (between b a c) ∧ |(b─a)| < |s|
text: This rule is not in [Avigad et al., 2009] but is convenient for proving some propositions.

name: point_in_circle_if
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ |(a─c)| < |(a─b)| → c.insideCircle α
text: If a is the centre of α and b is on α, and ac < ab if and only if c is in α. -- Given any points b and c, and circle C, such that b is on C and the straight-line from the centre of C to c is less than the straight-line from the centre of C to b, then c is inside the circle C.

name: point_in_circle_onlyif
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ (c.insideCircle α) → |(a─c)| < |(a─b)|
text: -- Given any points b and c, and circle C, such that b is on C and c is inside the circle C, then the straight-line from the centre of C to c is less than the straight-line from the centre of C to b.

name: point_on_circle_if
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ |(a─c)| = |(a─b)| → c.onCircle α
text: If a is the centre of α and b is on α, then ac = ab if and only if c is on α. If a point x is the centre of circle C and a point b is on C, then given some point c such that the straight-line from x to c is equal to the straight-line from x to b, then c is on C.

name: point_on_circle_onlyif
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle), (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle α) → |(a─c)| = |(a─b)|
text: If a point x is the centre of circle C and a point b is on C, then given some point c on C, the straight-line from x to c is equal to the straight-line from x to b

name: point_on_line_same_side
statement: ∀ (L M : Line) (b : Point), ¬(b.onLine L) ∧ (L.intersectsLine M) → ∃ a : Point, a.onLine M ∧ a.sameSide b L
text: A stronger version of the Points construction rule 6 in [Avigad et al., 2009], which is convenient for proving some propositions.

name: point_same_side
statement: ∀ (L : Line) (b : Point), ¬(b.onLine L) → ∃ a : Point, a.sameSide b L

name: quadrilateralAnglesSum
statement: (a b c d : Point) (AB CD AC BD : Line) : formQuadrilateral a b c d AB CD AC BD → ∠ a:b:d + ∠ b:d:c + ∠ d:c:a + ∠ c:a:b = ∟ + ∟ + ∟ + ∟

name: rectangle_area
statement: ∀ (a b c d : Point) (AB CD AC BD : Line), formParallelogram a b c d AB CD AC BD ∧ (∠ a:c:d = ∟) → (Triangle.area △ a:c:d + Triangle.area △ a:b:d = |(a─b)| * |(a─c)|) ∧ (Triangle.area △ b:a:c + Triangle.area △ b:d:c) = |(a─b)| * |(a─c)|
text: Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] but required by Proposition 47

name: same_side_not_on_line
statement: ∀ (a b : Point) (L : Line), a.sameSide b L → ¬(a.onLine L)
text: If a and b are on the same side of L, then a is not on L

name: same_side_pigeon_hole
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) ∧ ¬(b.onLine L) ∧ ¬(c.onLine L) → (a.sameSide b L) ∨ (a.sameSide c L) ∨ (b.sameSide c L)
text: If a, b, and c are not on L, and a and b are not on the same side of L, then either a and c are on the same side of L, or b and c are on the same side of L

name: same_side_rfl
statement: ∀ (a : Point) (L : Line), ¬(a.onLine L) → a.sameSide a L
text: same side axioms If a is not on L, then a and a are on the same side of L

name: same_side_symm
statement: ∀ (a b : Point) (L : Line), a.sameSide b L → b.sameSide a L
text: If a and b are on the same side of L, then b and a are on the same side of L

name: same_side_trans
statement: ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a.sameSide b L) ∧ (a.sameSide c L) → b.sameSide c L
text: If a and b are on the same side of L, and a and c are on the same side of L, then b and c are on the same side of L

name: segment_gte_zero
statement: ∀ (s : Segment), 0 ≤ s.length
text: ab ≥ 0 @[simp]

name: segment_symmetric
statement: ∀ (a b : Point), |(a─b)| = |(b─a)|
text: ab = ba. @[simp]

name: sum_angles_if
statement: ∀ (a b c d : Point) (L M : Line), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ ¬(d.onLine L) ∧ ¬(d.onLine M) ∧ (L ≠ M) ∧ (∠ b:a:c) = (∠ b:a:d) + (∠ d:a:c) → (b.sameSide d M) ∧ (c.sameSide d L)
text: -- Given points a, b and c such that a is not equal to b and a is not equal to c, and line L such that a and b are on L, and the angle formed by b:a:c has degree zero,  then c is on L and a is not between b and c. axiom degenerated_angle_onlyif : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line), (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (∠ b: a: c) = (0 : ℝ) → (c.onLine L) ∧ ¬(between b a c) Suppose a is on L and M, b is on L, c is on M, a != b, a != c, d is not on L or M, and L != M. Then \bac = \bad + \dac if and only if b and d are on the same side of M and c and d are on the same side of L. Given point on a given lines L and M, point b  on L, and point c on M with a distinct from b, a distinct from c, point d  not on L or M, and L distinct from M, then the angle bac is equal to the sum of angles bad and dac only if b and d are on the same side of M and c and d are on the same side of L. Kaiyu: Jeremy's typo here.

name: sum_angles_onlyif
statement: ∀ (a b c d : Point) (L M : Line),
text: Given point on a given lines L and M, point b  on L, and point c on M with a distinct from b, a distinct from c, point d  not on L or M, and L distinct from M, then b and d are on the same side of M and c and d are on the same side of L only if the angle bac is equal to the sum of angles bad and dac

name: sum_areas_if
statement: ∀ (a b c d : Point) (L : Line), (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ (b ≠ c) ∧ ¬(d.onLine L) ∧ (between a c b) → (Triangle.area △ a:c:d + Triangle.area △ d:c:b = Triangle.area △ a:d:b)
text: If a, b, c are all on a given line point L and distinct from one another, and d is not on L, and  c is  between a and b, then the sum of the areas of triangles acd and dcb is equal to the area of triangle adb

name: sum_areas_onlyif
statement: ∀ (a b c d : Point) (L : Line), (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ (b ≠ c) ∧ ¬(d.onLine L) ∧ (Triangle.area △ a:c:d + Triangle.area △ d:c:b = Triangle.area △ a:d:b) → between a c b
text: If a, b, c are all on a given line point L and distinct from one another, and d is not on L, and the sum of the areas of triangles acd and dcb is equal to the area of triangle adb, then c is between a and b.

name: sum_parallelograms_area
statement: ∀ (a b c d e f : Point) (AB CD AC BD : Line), formParallelogram a b c d AB CD AC BD ∧ between a e b ∧ between c f d → Triangle.area △ a:c:f + Triangle.area △ a:f:e + (Triangle.area △ e:f:d) + (Triangle.area △ e:d:b) = (Triangle.area △ a:c:d) + (Triangle.area △ a:d:b)
text: /-- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] -/ Given a parallelogram formed from points a, b, c and d, and given points e and f such that e is betwen a and b and f is between c and d, then the sum of the areas of the triangles acf, afe, efd, and edb is equal to the sum of the areas of triangles acd and adb

name: superposition
statement: ∀ (a b c d g h : Point) (AB BC AC L : Line), formTriangle a b c AB BC AC ∧ distinctPointsOnLine d g L ∧ ¬(h.onLine L) → ∃ (b' c' : Point) (BC' AC' : Line), (∠ b:a:c : ℝ) = (∠ b':d:c') ∧ (∠ a:c:b : ℝ) = (∠ d:c':b') ∧ (∠ c:b:a : ℝ) = (∠ c':b':d) ∧ |(a─b)| = |(d─b')| ∧ |(b─c)| = |(b'─c')| ∧ |(c─a)| = |(c'─d)| ∧ b'.onLine L ∧ ¬(between b' d g) ∧ c'.sameSide h L ∧ distinctPointsOnLine b' c' BC' ∧ distinctPointsOnLine d c' AC'
text: A combination of the two superposition rules in [Avigad et al., 2009]

name: triple_incidence_1
statement: ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ (b.sameSide c N) → ¬(b.sameSide d M)
text: triple incidence axioms If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, and b and c are on the same side of N, then b and d are not on the same side of M

name: triple_incidence_2
statement: ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ ¬(b.sameSide d M) ∧ ¬(d.onLine M) ∧ (b ≠ a) → b.sameSide c N
text: If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, and b and d are not on the same side of M, and d is not on M and b != a, then b and c are on the same side of N

name: triple_incidence_3
statement: ∀ (L M N : Line) (a b c d e : Point), (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (a.onLine N) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine M) ∧ (d.onLine N) ∧ (c.sameSide d L) ∧ (b.sameSide c N) ∧ (d.sameSide e M) ∧ (c.sameSide e N) → c.sameSide e L
text: If L, M, and N are lines meeting at a point a, and b, c, and d are points on L, M, and N respectively, and if c and d are on the same side of L, and b and c are on the same side of N, and d and e are on the same side of M, and c and e are on the same side of N, then c and e are on the same side of L

name: two_points_determine_line
statement: ∀ (a b : Point) (L M : Line), distinctPointsOnLine a b L ∧ (a.onLine M) ∧ (b.onLine M) → L = M
text: If points `a` and `b` are distinct, and both points are on lines `L` and `M`, then `L = M`

name: zero_segment_if
statement: ∀ (a b : Point), |(a ─ b)| = 0 → a = b
text: Metric inferences defined in Sec. 3.5 of Avigad et al., 2009 Generally speaking, they are not used explicitly in the tactics written by humans. + is associative and commutative, with identity 0. < is a linear ordering with least element 0 For any x, y, and z, if x < y then x + z < y + z ab = 0 if and only if a = b.
